items.name: permission-editor
items.title: Permission Editor
items.description: A controlled permission workspace with category navigation, application-owned menu trees, compact action tiles and named data scopes.
items.docs: The application owns the exposed permission catalog, its business grouping, labels and persistence. Pass sections of groups of rows; the component has no built-in business or system permissions and never discovers or requests them. Preserve caller action order, including non-CRUD operations. Each row shows a checkbox, its title and optional hint; enabled scoped actions show every independently named range directly. onEnabledChange and onLevelChange report only explicit draft edits by stable row or scope id. The host owns loading, validation, Save, conflicts and preservation of grants absent from the visible catalog. Installing a plugin or receiving a capability in options does not opt it into this form: select only actual application features and supported actions in application-owned composition code. Settings require explicit app opt-in, an actual registered configuration page and matching server capability/action together; neither installed plugins nor a catalog entry alone are sufficient. Keep the original category navigation (left-side desktop, horizontal narrow layout), show one category by default and matching categories during global filtering; search and enabled-only filters never change grants. Do not supply a default System and tools section or copy demo permissions into an application. Set group.accessOnly for a page with one access action. Supply scope.configuration for parameterized filters, scope.hint for contextual help, and translated labels including emptyDescription, readOnly and managedPermission. Full-width descriptions use LongText and narrow tile descriptions use LongTextPreview; disabled controls have visible explanations. Existing apps reconcile the component, its LongText and Empty dependencies, application catalog adapter and host bindings through a normal source upgrade. Preserve unknown policies and native filter parameters. For page access, pass section.navigation as application-owned nodes with id, label, optional rowId and children. References use the existing flat row ids; a structural menu group has no grant. Single-level menus stay flat; a parent page and its children use independent checkboxes for staged authorization. Disclosure only changes presentation. Search includes ancestor names and retains their paths; filtering expands matching branches and Clear restores collapse state. The host adapter uses the complete runtime menu tree and its navigation transforms, deduplicates inherited page grants, and retains independent non-menu pages. Supply translated expandGroup and collapseGroup callbacks. Never infer authorization inheritance or grant every child when opening a menu group. All page grants, business actions and settings permissions use Checkbox to edit the host draft. The enabled-only filter also uses Checkbox and changes presentation immediately without editing grants. The page-access tree contains business pages only. Compose every actual system-settings page and operation, including user management and business configuration, under Configuration permissions. Preserve original row ids and grants when reclassifying existing controls, and do not duplicate these entries as page checkboxes or category-jump placeholders. Explain this boundary in the application-supplied section descriptions.

items.name: role-list
items.title: Role List
items.description: A role administration table built with the standard DataTable: localized column headers, sortable names and identifiers, protected/custom badges, and pagination. The host supplies authorized rows and edit destinations. Preinstalled in both application templates.
items.docs: Render inside a React Router and the application i18n provider. Supply roles with key, localized title, edit destination (to) and protected state. Pass localized labels for name, key, type, protected and custom, plus an optional ariaLabel. Uses the shared DataTable for table semantics, sorting and pagination. The host owns loading, empty/error states, filtering and authorization. Existing apps must update the installed role-list component, its data-table dependency and caller labels together.

items.name: default-access-editor
items.title: Default Access Editor
items.description: Controlled default data scope fields grouped by operation, with independently named ranges and native custom-filter slots. The host supplies localized business captions, current rules and authorized writes.
items.docs: Pass localized labels, a stable rule key, resource choices and scope controls. Explain that default data scopes combine with role-granted scopes for users who already hold the operation permission, and that restriction rules still constrain final access. The host loads authorization/defaultAccess and authorization/defaultAccess/options, enforces settings:authorization.default-access read/create/update/delete, and owns draft preservation, custom filters, validation, confirmation and writes. Existing apps reconcile the editor, default-access pages/model/routes, locales from the updated template. No existing rule is seeded or rewritten on upgrade. Both templates expose one Permission management sidebar entry with Roles and permissions and Default data scopes tabs, without changing their route ids, URLs, settings guards or stored rules. This navigation organization does not add sharing or restriction editors. Keep global default data scopes in the Permission management tabs and omit the contextual shortcut from role editors to avoid confusing global rules with the current role’s scopes. Group scopes with the same stable actionId under one operation heading; each scope retains its independent id, selection, filter and error. The application shares scope captions with its role permission adapter rather than exposing collection identifiers, and preserves original resource/action/scope keys and stored rules.
